reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown read the lying spirit as God overruling Satan's evil for righteous judgment, not God himself originating a lie.

discrepancy.note: Ingersoll counts the lying spirit sent to deceive Ahab's prophets among the ways Jehovah is shown breaking his own commandment against false witness.

quotes.text: "Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbor," and yet he sent abroad "lying spirits" to deceive his own prophets, and in a hundred ways paid tribute to deceit.
quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), The Christian Religion, pt. III (Rejoinder to Judge Black) (1881), on 1 Kings 22:23.

sides.snippet: God is not a man, that he should lie
sides.verseText: God is not a man, that he should lie, Neither the son of man, that he should repent: Has he said, and will he not do it? Or has he spoken, and will he not make it good?

sides.snippet: Yahweh has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these your prophets
sides.verseText: Now therefore, behold, Yahweh has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these your prophets; and Yahweh has spoken evil concerning you.
